clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented with palpitations and discomfort during swallowing. Initial chest radiograph and subsequent CT scan revealed a large, lobulated mediastinal mass (75 × 57 × 80 mm) compressing the esophagus. Surgical excision of the mass was performed, which necessitated a subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy due to an extensive defect. Histopathological examination of the excised mass showed spindle-shaped cells with a fasciculated and disarrayed architecture, nuclei in a palisading pattern, and S100 protein positivity, establishing the diagnosis of benign schwannoma. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, with no evidence of recurrence to date.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with palpitations and discomfort during swallowing.
Initial chest radiograph showed a smooth, round mass, slightly larger than 7 cm in diameter, in the middle mediastinum between the trachea and vertebral bodies.
Chest CT scan showed a lobulated tumor (75 × 57 × 80 mm) in the upper to middle mediastinum, with a homogenous inner component, compressing the esophagus.

During surgery, a mass slightly larger than 8 cm in diameter was found adjacent to the mid-thoracic esophagus and excised. Due to an extensive defect in the adventitia and muscular layer, subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy were performed.
Histopathological examination revealed spindle-shaped cells in a fasciculated and disarrayed architecture and nuclei in a palisading pattern.
Immunohistochemical studies revealed S100 protein positivity.
The histopathological and immunohistochemical findings established the diagnosis of benign schwannoma.
Postoperative course was uneventful with no evidence of recurrence.
